title: Topics in Comparative Politics; Gender and Security in Conflict and Post-Conflict Societies
description: This course looks at the ways in which gender shapes politics and political outcomes during and after conflict. The course is designed for students who are motivated to think critically about a range of issues related to gender and conflict in the international context. It introduces students to feminist theoretical frameworks for thinking about politics, as well as to empirical explorations of a variety of key topics within the larger field of gender and politics. These topics include women's political participation and representation during and after conflict, women in war and peacekeeping, their experiences with war, human rights, and globalization, and legal norms that have been diffused by the UN system.
